content: 1. Tobramycin can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity when used concurrently with amphotericin B deoxycholate. Avoid or consider alternative therapy to mitigate this risk. 2. Tobramycin enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Co-administration of tobramycin and bacitracin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or consider alternative therapy. 4. Bacitracin should not be used concurrently with other nephrotoxic drugs, including tobramycin, to prevent additive toxic effects. 5. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 6. Bumetanide and tobramycin together increase the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, and do not administer the vaccine within 14 days of antibiotic use. 8. Cidofovir and tobramycin both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or consider alternative therapy. 9. Tobramycin enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Ethacrynic acid and tobramycin together increase the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Furosemide and tobramycin together increase the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Mannitol increases tobramycin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 14. Neomycin (oral) and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid or consider alternative therapy. 15. Tobramycin enhances the effects of pancuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Quinidine increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Tobramycin enhances the effects of rapacuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Tobramycin enhances the effects of rocuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Tobramycin enhances the effects of succinylcholine through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Torsemide and tobramycin together increase the risk of ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of the typhoid vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 22. Tobramycin enhances the effects of vecuronium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of apnea. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Tobramycin enhances the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 24. Acyclovir and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Amikacin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Amiodarone increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of oral forms of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 28. Capreomycin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Carboplatin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cefaclor increases the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of tobramycin. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cephalosporins, including cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefiderocol, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftazidime/avibactam, ceftibuten, ceftizoxime, ceftobiprole medocaril sodium, ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, and cephalexin, increase the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of tobramycin. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cephaloridine and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Cisplatin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Clarithromycin increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Clotrimazole decreases tobramycin levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Colistin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of oral forms of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 38. Iodinated contrast media and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Cyclosporine and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Tobramycin decreases its own levels while increasing daptomycin levels when co-administered. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Tobramycin enhances the effects of daxibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 42. Deferasirox and tobramycin together increase the risk of acute renal failure. Monitor serum creatinine and/or creatinine clearance in patients receiving both drugs concomitantly. 43. Dichlorphenamide and tobramycin both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Tobramycin increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Dronedarone increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Tobramycin and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of oral forms of estradiol, estrogens (conjugated synthetic), and estropipate by altering intestinal flora. These interactions pose a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 49. Felodipine increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Fosphenytoin decreases tobramycin levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Gentamicin and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Tobramycin enhances the effects of incobotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 53. Indinavir increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Ioversol and tobramycin together increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 55. Ketoconazole increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Tobramycin enhances the effects of letibotulinumtoxinA through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor for excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. 57. Levoketoconazole increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Loratadine increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Magnesium supplements and tobramycin together enhance each other’s neuromuscular blocking effects, potentially causing negative respiratory effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Tobramycin reduces the efficacy of oral forms of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 61. Nefazodone increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Nicardipine increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Nifedipine decreases tobramycin levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Nilotinib increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely.
